utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Just before we go for the next witness, the Trial Chamber has one or two housekeeping matters to address in relation to three exhibits, each of which consists of a very lengthy document or a book. On the 30th of January and on the 3rd of March, and on the 4th of May, 2006, three books were admitted into evidence as Exhibits 24, 238, and 476 respectively. The Trial Chamber notes that there is a significant discrepancy between the very few portions put by the parties to the witnesses in court and the English and B/C/S portions respectively which form part of the trial record. The Trial Chamber is of the view that it is essential for a fair and expeditious trial to preserve a coherent and clean trial record. The Trial Chamber therefore orders as follows: That each party shall indicate which pages of the three books it wishes to tender into evidence by Friday, the 26th of May, 2006, based upon the examination-in-chief, cross-examination, or re-examination as applicable, which it carried out in relation to the books. 2: Each party shall properly scan only the portions sought to be admitted and resubmit them to the Registrar in English and B/C/S by Friday the 26th of May, 2006. And 3: The Registrar shall correct the trial record and assign any new exhibit numbers necessary out of court.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for clarity for this project, am I to understand from -- I'm sorry, from the first point, that the parties are limited in tendering only those portions of the books which were actually discussed during examination, cross-examination or re-examination? Because it had been my intention, based on the Court's decision of the 19th of May, 2006, which also addresses this issue, to do precisely this exercise but I was not intending to limit it to -- in that way. I was going to, rather, select the portions which I thought might be of relevance to the issues in the trial, and I was going to go by that guideline rather than the guideline which is -- unless -- which has perhaps just been suggested by the Trial Chamber. Or maybe I misunderstood what the Trial Chamber is saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No. You don't seem to have misunderstood. This guideline, this latest one that we have just read now is inspired by a belief that, from the point of view of the parties, that which was of interest to them in those documents was that which was canvassed in court. It was not anticipated that there were other materials in the same documents beyond what was canvassed in court that was seen to be as relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, I can say I know -- I know that one of the books - and I think it's the last one, from the 4th of May, Exhibit 476 - I believe, if my recollection is correct, that this is the book of Borislav Jovic and it is a very lengthy book and there are lots of portions which are not of relevance to the Trial Chamber. However, I put that into evidence through a witness, through Mr. Kerkkanen, who really was, as we know, kind of an authenticating witness and just for relevance, to show that at least the document was relevant to the trial, and to some degree I did highlight two or so passages, maybe more, maybe three passages of the book that were relevant. However, I didn't -- I did not go through the exercise of going through every passage in the book which might be of relevance. Which does not equal the entire book. So what I would like to be able to do, if the Trial Chamber is agreeable, is to -- for purposes of this exercise, is to identify the portions of the book which I think might be relevant to the Trial Chamber, to the issues, and of assistance to the Trial Chamber which -- but which may not necessarily have been discussed in court. Frankly, if -- I could have gone through page after page after page of the book with the witness. All he could have said is that -- is what's on the book. He couldn't have really added much more comment than that and it would have taken an enormous amount of time. I'm not sure it would have been of any assistance or added any value to go through that exercise. Now that we have the book available, I would like, if the Court is agreeable, to identify only the relevant portions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me understand. You asked the witness about the contents of that book to show the relevance of the book to the issues of this matter, in this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, to show the relevance of at least parts of the book, in order to satisfy our burden of showing, before we admit -- seek admission into evidence of a document, that it's relevant to the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So I did that with respect to -- I picked three excerpts from the book but I didn't pick every excerpt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But do those three excerpts, did they not accomplish your mission, to show its relevance?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It -- I think it accomplishes the mission to show the relevance to get the document into evidence, but I think it would be unfortunate if the Trial Chamber were then limited in its examination to just those three excerpts and did not have available to it other portions of the book which would be relevant to the issues of the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I would imagine --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And I think it would -- I understand the Court doesn't want the record to be burdened with documentation that is not relevant to the trial, and that is excessive, and I'll keep that in mind and try to be extremely selective and only select portions which would be of relevance to the issues before the Trial Chamber, and I think it would -- it won't be -- it will be far from the whole book. It's only going to be a portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But if it's 50 per cent of the book and that 50 per cent of the book only demonstrates the relevance and relevance can be demonstrated by the three excerpts that you have referred to in your examination, the question is how -- what does the rest of the portion that you want to put in, what does it achieve?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, they are relevant to other issues because the book, as you'll recall, is the diary of Borislav Jovic, who was the Serbian representative on the Presidency of the SFRY and himself the president of the Presidency for an important period of time, and a very close ally of Slobodan Milosevic. And he writes about the events that occur -- he writes to some extent about events occurring in the Krajina in Croatia, and I picked out I think it's three entries, but there are several other entries which are relevant to events. And my guess is that the Defence will also have the same view of this, that they will find entries in that same book which they might think will be of relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's hear what the Defence has got to say. Mr. Milovancevic, do you have any response to make?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence agrees with what the Prosecutor has said. We feel that this is a situation which might be limiting both for the Prosecution and the Defence, if we were to strictly adhere to Your Honour's instruction, not just with respect to these three books but perhaps with respect to other documents also. A number of other issues might arise which have not yet been touched on, either in the work of the Prosecution or the work of the Defence. That is why I share my learned friend's opinion that perhaps this kind of guideline from the Trial Chamber would limit both the Defence and the Prosecution in their work. And another issue arises here, Your Honour. The opposite side could always object that something has been taken out of context if something were extracted, and this should be borne in mind, perhaps. But I do support what my learned friend has said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Sorry, wouldn't you have had your opportunity in cross-examination, when the book was being put to the witness, to give evidence concerning it, and through whom it was tendered, essentially? Wouldn't that have been your opportunity in respect of anything that was in the book that was contrary to what the witness said? And if the book is in fact ever-present and you need it in the future, either the Prosecution or the Defence, through a witness, are you not still able to use the book to do effectively what you want to do? I'm asking Mr. Milovancevic firstly but I'd also like to hear Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if it is the position of the Trial Chamber that the book can be used to introduce certain facts through other witnesses and raise other relevant issues, then the Defence would be satisfied at present, but listening to my learned friend, I was concerned that we might arrive at a situation where a certain book was marked as an exhibit and relevant topics extracted and we would then be deprived of the opportunity of using parts of the book further in the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me understand you clearly, Mr. Milovancevic. I hear you say you support your learned friend. However, what you say in support of that seems -- comes across as slightly different. Your learned friend's position is he's agreeable to reducing the entire book, but not limiting it to just what was discussed in court. He would like to be able to include a few more pages or a few more parts of the book that were not necessarily discussed. Now, is that what you are supporting?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, precisely so, Your Honour. Thank you for putting it so precisely. That is just what I wanted to say and what I think my learned friend has said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. In the interests of expediency, we will lift this order for now. We will not put it into operation, and we will discuss it and we'll come back at the next session with a reasoned answer. Thank you very much. I don't know whether I say Ms. Richterova or I should address Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll be handling the next witness. If I may just -- if it's of assistance, because I know the Court is going to be considering it, Judge Nosworthy invited -- I've been waiting for the opportunity to pronounce the name correctly and I've just had it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Whiting. Finally.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And I apologise again for previous mispronunciations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Just to respond to Your Honour's question, I'm not sure that we have future witnesses who will be able to -- because we are coming kind of to the end of our Prosecution case and hadn't anticipated this issue, so that's another reason why we would ask to be allowed to put in other portions of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We will consider that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Our next witness is MM-078. I think Ms. Richterova would like to be excused, if she may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sure Ms. Richterova is going to speak for herself.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you. The senior trial attorney likes talking on my behalf.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: He doesn't want you in court when he's doing his job.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So may I be excused, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're quite excused, Ms. Richterova. Thank you very much. MM-078, you said. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the witness please make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I notice the curtain is down. There was a distortion of the face. Is this a protected witness? Do we need to be in any kind of closed or private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Not at the moment, Your Honour. I believe the booth is aware that this witness has protective measures and so face distortion has been accomplished, and this stays down and there are -- nobody is allowed in there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed. And may the witness please be seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, you may sit down. Good afternoon, sir. First of all, can you hear me and understand me in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-078
utterances.text: I can hear you very well and I can follow what you're saying in a language that I can understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, if at any time you cannot hear me or you cannot understand me or anybody else in the courtroom, please let us know. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-078
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I first want to apologise for the long time that you've been waiting. We had expected to start your testimony earlier today and there was a delay this morning and so I know that this has resulted in you waiting a long time and I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-078
utterances.text: I accept your apology.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could I first, with the assistance of the usher, show the witness the pseudonym sheet, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, without saying the name, can you look at that name and tell us if that is your name on that sheet with the number MM-078?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-078
utterances.text: Yes. This is my name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-078
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is my name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could that please be shown to the Defence and then to the Trial Chamber. And could that be made an exhibit, under seal, please, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May this document please be made an exhibit. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Exhibit number will be 720, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, Witness, as you know, you have been granted certain protective measures for your testimony here during this trial, and I just want to go over them with you. The first is that you will be referred to by pseudonym, and the pseudonym is MM-078, though often we will just call you "Witness." You will -- your image also will not be broadcast as part of this proceeding, and in addition, if we discuss any details or information that might identify you, that will be done in private session and there will be no broadcast of that testimony. Do you understand all those measures?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-078
utterances.text: I do, and I thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And I'll remind you that you have a glass of water there, and if at any time you need to have a drink, please do.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-078
utterances.text: I thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could we go into private session, please, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 24th day of May, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.48 p.m.,
